fix0.summary:
I fixed all six round-3 findings of WP-51 at their root causes. Each fix has a test that fails without it: 19 mutants, one per fix plus the five survivors of finding 5 and the five of minor 4, are each killed by the suite. Every scoped check passes. Nothing was committed, and only internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/ was touched.

F1 (blocker): patterns are now measured before anything compiles them, in the new file patternsize.go.
- The walk no longer calls regexp.Compile. It parses each pattern and patternProperties name and counts the program the way Go's own parser estimates it, every copy of a repetition included.
- RZ-CFG-005 caps a pattern at MaxPatternInstructions (2^14) and a document at MaxDocumentInstructions (2^17), per decision 14.
- Two parser costs are bounded before the parse:
  - The ranges of each Unicode class escape count toward the program, five ranges per instruction. 16,000 \pL escapes are only 16,002 instructions, yet they took 0.9 s and kept 166 MB.
  - Case-insensitive class ranges are capped at maxFoldRunes per document, because Go folds them one character at a time: about 3 ms per wide range.
- The regexp matcher is now charged only where a pattern may reach a value or a member name. A {} body under a large pattern reserves a few KB instead of 64 MB.
- Benchmarks: the largest patterns compile in 0.11 s and 900 \pL escapes in 0.14 s.

F3: new ReservationFactor = 12 (decision 13).
- Decoded values plus their map, array and string overhead plus the decision working set over 12x maxRequestBodyBytes is 413 (errReservationTooLarge) before Reserve.
- A failing body whose location pass would pass 12x gets DetailMismatch alone.

F4: each evaluation with contains is charged 16 bytes per item on the path. Those with minContains or maxContains are charged it again in the location tree, which keeps the list.

F5: propertyNames wrappers are charged one per applying evaluation, and only for names that can fail. A valid 64% map under propertyNames now passes.

F2: I made only the sound tightenings available:
- The call stack and the scope walks hold one chain of in-place evaluations per value, not every evaluation. A 14 KB rich-text body now reserves 0.55 MB of stack instead of 29 MB; stackBytes is now 8 KiB per chain frame, checked with debug.SetMaxStack.
- A lower and an upper bound that cannot both fail count once.
- An integer literal never fails an integer type.

doc.go now states the measured fit. TestHandleMeasuredFit pins admitted fractions for 8- and 20-way unions, rich text, component trees, GeoJSON and a map under propertyNames; the reservation limit is pinned by TestHandleReservationLimit.

F6: I added the five regression tests:
- an array-valued const or enum gives DetailNumber;
- the dynamic-scope doubling schema is refused at /oneOf;
- prefixItems plus contains is refused at /contains;
- queueBound is checked on a sparse anchored alternation;
- the crossing depth of 10 is pinned.

Minors:
- 0: the disjoint-pattern over-approximation is documented and pinned in TestEvaluationBound.
- 1: added Schema.ValidateWithin(v, rawLimit), which applies Handle's limits except the reservation.
- 2 and 3: become contract requests, since the hub and the executor are outside WP-51.
- 4: all five model terms are pinned.
- 5: the sampled-peak thresholds are widened.
- 6: all leftovers are cleaned up; keywordPointer moved into the test file.

lenses.summary:
Round-4 review of WP-51 (internal/filter/validation/jsonschema), lens: resource bounds and hostile inputs, judged against the R-77/user decisions in w3-s2-wp51-r3.json and 00-architecture.md. I measured Factory.Build and Handle at the 10 MiB default through -overlay probes in scratch (repo untouched; baseline suite passes, 47s).

The three round-3 fixes I could directly attack all hold: F1 regex program cap refuses the \pL flood (16,000 escapes -> "more than 16384 instructions", 5ms) and near-2^14 repetitions compile in ~29ms; the escape-range and maxFoldRunes bounds work and are approved per the decisions. F4 (contains matched-index lists) and F5 (propertyNames wrappers) are complete: location/decision trees stay within charge (e.g. contains-100 chain over 16,000 items: location tree 12.7MB vs charge 25.9MB; the valid 450k-member map under propertyNames maxLength now fits at 50% instead of 413). F3 caps the reservation at 12x (request side <=13x). All five round-3 F6 mutants now have regression tests (W14 in TestHandleNumberPaths with array-valued const/enum + out-of-range numbers; K2/K14b in TestEvaluationBound; R1 in TestQueueBoundBudget's sparse anchored alternation; X15 in TestCrossingDepth pinning depth 10).

Resource accounting is sound: I found NO under-reservation (reserved >= live decoded tree across member counts 1..100 and all TestHandleReservesDecodedMaps shapes; unevaluated chains over-reserve 3-6x peak), NO unbounded CPU (pattern matches on 2MB hostile strings and contains-chains stay ~0.5-0.9 ns per model unit counting both passes; work limit ~2.7s), and NO false refusal of ordinary valid bodies beyond the R-77-accepted consequences (dense small-object/enum/union arrays, uniqueItems object arrays, deep recursive docs). Deep nesting is handled safely (decode rejects >64 levels; the nesting-limit 413 reserves nothing). Content keywords are annotation-only (no AssertContent/AssertFormat), so no hidden recursion. Over-reservation of unions/recursive documents (3.5-27x peak) is the documented, user-accepted R-77 consequence, not a finding.

One genuine, previously-unflagged minor: foldsCase over-approximates case folding (treats (?-i) and scoped (?i:) as global folding), which can falsely refuse an exotic but legal case-sensitive pattern at compile. It is conservative (never under-counts), so it breaks no resource bound. No blocker or major findings; WP-51 is ready to land.

Verdict: fix. There is one blocker, and it means round-3 F1 (the regex program cap) is not fully fixed. No repository file was changed. My probes ran from scratch through go test -overlay (scratchpad r4int/p), and git status is unchanged.

The blocker: a ladder of references into positions outside the keyword tree makes the library meta-validate the same subtree, and recompile every pattern in it, about 59 times. Accepted schemas then take 2 to 5 s and allocate over 2 GB to compile in both Check and Factory.Build. That breaks 07 F6's 1 s bound, WP-51's Done-when ("compile budget met") and doc.go's compile figures. Compiling the reference-only positions outermost-first fixes it.

The minor findings: the unapproved maxFoldRunes cap refuses an ordinary 263-byte schema, and carry-over reuse depends on the order WP-70 builds Policies in.

Checked and correct:
- **Shapes and errors:** Factory.Build matches filter.Factory, and its errors carry RZ-CFG-005 through errcode.Wrap. Shared errors pass through uncoded, as the engineer's contract request says. Check matches hub.PolicyCheck, with Field/Index paths under spec.config.schema and a nil loc handled. Repeated runs give the same diagnostics.
- **Executor mapping:** the CannotDecide causes wrap filter.ErrTooLarge and ErrBudget, which internal/gateway/executor/cursor.go maps to 413 RZ-RT-003 and 503 RZ-RT-004 under either failureMode.
- **Budget:** Handle checks the 12x reservation limit and ctx before it reserves. Both reservations (the decision pass and the location pass's extra) are released by defer on every path, including library panics and a failed Reserve. This matches body.Account semantics.
- **Sharing across goroutines:** the shared Schema is read-only at run time (bodyScan and the evalState lookups mutate nothing), and the library builds a fresh validator per call. The race run passes.
- **Decision wrapper:** I probed schemas whose $id is decide.json or policy.json, embedded $id resources and $dynamicAnchor roots; valid and invalid bodies are all decided correctly. The library's bool mode exits early only after an error, so the two passes cannot disagree on validity.
- **Imports and dependencies:** imports are the architecture 1.2 row plus errcode and phase, which the engineer raised as a contract request. Neither drivers nor JOSE code are linked.
- **Checks run:** CGO_ENABLED=0 tests with -shuffle pass, as do -race tests (53 s). golangci-lint run reports 0 issues, fmt --diff is clean, go vet passes and repocheck passes.

The other round-3 fixes hold for the cases they targeted: F3's 12x reservation cap, F4's contains lists, F5's propertyNames wrappers and F6's regression tests. The ctx-canceled and Check-memo minors remain contract requests, as the engineer stated.

WP-51 round 4 should not land yet: one blocker and one major remain.

**Required checks:** all pass. Build and vet are clean. `go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on` passes (158 s, 97.9% coverage), as do `CGO_ENABLED=0` (44 s) and `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` (46 s). Each fuzz target ran 75 s with no failure (FuzzCompileSchema, FuzzValidate, FuzzDifferential), on a scratch copy of the repository so no corpus could be written into it. `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues, `golangci-lint fmt --diff` is clean, and repocheck passes.

**Load:** four concurrent runs of the sampled-peak tests (`-test.count=3`, plus two busy loops) all passed.

**Round-3 fixes:**
- F3 (reservation cap at 12 times the limit), F4 (contains matched lists), F5 (propertyNames wrappers) and F6 (surviving mutants) are fixed and pinned. Re-mutating W14, R1, MK (propertyNames wrappers), ML (in-place chains) and MN (minContains matches) makes the suite fail as it should.
- The kindInteger and paired-bound tightenings are sound against the library code.
- TestStackWithinCharge works: it fails when the stack limit is set to a third of the charge and passes at two thirds, and its `-cover` run passes.
- The F2(b), F2(c) and F2(e) deviations match the R-77 decisions.

**Blocker (incomplete F1 fix):** `walker.pattern` keeps calling `syntax.Parse` on every pattern after the document instruction bound is exceeded. fix.summary:
WP-51 round 9: the blocker, the major finding and the visible minor findings are fixed. The code changes stay inside internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/, and every scoped check passes.

Blocker (one-pass matcher tables):
- Root cause: Go's regexp builds one-pass tables for any program that is anchored at begin-text and has fewer than 1,000 instructions. Those tables copy every instruction and every class's ranges, and at each alternation they merge the first ranges of all branches, so they grow with the square of the alternation.
- Fix: the package's regexp engine (regexpCache → compilePattern in patternsize.go) compiles every pattern behind an empty group, `(?:)`. The program then starts with a no-op, so Go never builds the one-pass matcher.
  - Matching is unchanged. The empty group matches the empty string, and StartCond still sees the pattern as anchored.
  - compilePattern first parses the expression on its own, so an invalid pattern fails with Go's own error. FuzzCompilePattern found the case that needs this: `(?)*`, which the empty group would otherwise turn into a valid expression.
  - A compiledPattern wrapper's String() returns the expression as the schema wrote it, so keyword locations and sorting are unchanged.
- The measure in patternsize.go now counts what the compiled pattern keeps, in 40-byte instructions:
  - the instructions Go's parser estimates, every copy included;
  - each class's ranges, counted once, since copies share them;
  - 3 for each literal or class node, which the program may keep alive;
  - a 24-instruction overhead per pattern;
  - the parser's work, as before.
- Measured results:
  - All four review documents now compile and keep 3.5 to 5.6 MB at the document bound. They kept 185 MB (23 anchored alternations of 330 classes), 142 MB (alt131), 21 MB (131 four-range class repetitions) and 19 MB (8 x ^\pL{1,115}$).
  - With the empty group removed, the same tests keep 0.07 to 1.06 GB, so the tests fail without the fix.
- New tests:
  - TestPatternProgramMemory: every pattern-filled document stays at most 8 MiB. A document with MaxSubschemas positions plus patterns stays at most 16 MiB.
  - TestCompilePatternMatches: differential matching against Go's regexp, matching errors, and the program's start instruction.
  - FuzzCompilePattern: a new fuzz target.
  - The cases are also in BenchmarkCompileAnalysisWorstCase.

Pattern work model:
- While calibrating, I found that repetitions of large classes ran at up to about 1.5 to 1.8 ns per work unit. This predates the round.
- regexcost.go now charges 2 units per queue entry, per input byte and per search step in the program's largest class (classSteps). It also models the engine's program, which has one extra no-op instruction.
- BenchmarkPatternModel now has \pL and 4,096-range cases and stays at or below 0.63 ns per unit.

Major (member-name hashing):
- bodyScan.object now charges 1 unit per 8 bytes of each member name for:
  - each evaluation with member keywords (the properties lookup);
  - 5 per unevaluated copy;
  - each uniqueItems pass, once plus twice the bits of the member count (the sort);
  - each uniqueItems comparison.
- It also charges the object's longest name once per const or enum object compared with it. A new count dimension, dimObjects, carries that count, inherited through enclosing values.
- workWeight now also charges the bytes of required and dependency names that an evaluation looks up.
- BenchmarkWorkModel has four long-name cases at 0.03 to 0.26 ns per unit; every case is at most 0.75.

The matcher charge covers the backtracker's visited bit set (at most 32 KiB) and the NFA queues, but not the backtracker's job stack. Go uses the backtracker for every program of at most 500 instructions whenever the string or member name is shorter than 262,144/len(prog) bytes. The job stack holds one 16-byte job per alternation state on the current search path and can grow to about 2^17 to 2^18 jobs; with append growth the old and new arrays are live together, so the peak is about 4 to 7 MB per match, while the charge stays at 32 KiB + 64 bytes per instruction (about 33 to 64 KB).
